summary: Configured sudo on node1 to log every sudo invocation (user, timestamp, PWD, command) to a dedicated /var/log/sudo-commands.log via an /etc/sudoers.d/99-command-logging drop-in (Defaults logfile=..., log_input/log_output, !syslog), which also suppresses sudo's normal syslog/authpriv output so entries no longer land in the general system log (/var/log/secure). Verified before and after a full node reboot: dedicated log captured new sudo commands, secure log's sudo-line count stayed flat (14→14 pre-restart, 44→44 post-restart), and the node's boot id changed (4cee4ea8... → 772e50f6...) confirming an actual restart with the config surviving it.
actions_performed: Captured baseline: boot id, sudo version, existing sudoers.d contents, /var/log/secure presence, journald/rsyslog status
Created /etc/sudoers.d/99-command-logging with Defaults logfile=/var/log/sudo-commands.log, log_input/log_output, iolog_dir, and !syslog to suppress general-log duplication
Validated syntax with visudo -cf and set safe ownership/permissions on the drop-in and the new log file
Ran a test sudo command and confirmed it appeared in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user/timestamp/command, while /var/log/secure's sudo line count stayed unchanged
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect), polled until exec was available again
Confirmed boot id changed post-restart, re-validated sudoers drop-in, ran another sudo command, and confirmed it logged to the dedicated file with no new entries in /var/log/secure

evidence.requirement: Sudo commands are logged with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: Dedicated log shows entries like 'Sep 29 08:17:22 : root : PWD=/ ; USER=root ; ... COMMAND=/bin/id' both before and after restart

evidence.requirement: Sudo entries are kept out of the general system log
evidence.summary: /var/log/secure sudo-line count stayed identical (14->14 pre-restart, 44->44 post-restart) after new sudo commands were run, confirming !syslog suppressed the duplicate general-log entries

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot id 4cee4ea8-4b8e-4c2f-af1a-3a82b9ec41f4 and confirmed sudoers config valid and log active immediately before reboot

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: acknowledgement returns before disconnect
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot launched in background with 1s delay; exec call returned 'reboot issued' successfully before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: changed boot identity proves actual restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot id 772e50f6-002b-4be2-9e2e-a3d2cab6a183 differs from pre-restart 4cee4ea8-4b8e-4c2f-af1a-3a82b9ec41f4

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: recovered state and functionality verified
evidence.summary: Post-restart: sudoers drop-in still present/valid, dedicated log still capturing new sudo commands, general system log still receiving zero sudo entries
